mainTopic: The differences between money cases and capital cases in the משנה, and the גמרא's question of whether money cases truly require careful questioning of witnesses.
overview: The משנה opens by saying that money cases (דיני ממונות) and capital cases (דיני נפשות) share one rule: the witnesses must be carefully questioned (דרישה וחקירה), because the פסוק says 'you shall have one law.' It then lists the differences between the two kinds of cases. These cover the number of judges, how the discussion opens, the majority needed, and reopening a case. They also cover who may argue and switching sides, timing rules (including no capital trials on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב), which judge speaks first, and who is fit to judge. In each difference, capital cases lean toward saving the accused. The גמרא then asks whether money cases really need careful questioning. It points to a ברייתא that keeps a loan document valid even when its witnesses seem to have been elsewhere on its date. After explaining why it chose that ברייתא over a משנה about postdated documents, the גמרא brings the first of several answers (memory aid חרפ״ש). רבי חנינא says the Torah requires questioning in all cases, but the חכמים dropped it in money cases so lenders will not stop lending. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to challenge this answer, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Money cases and capital cases both require careful questioning of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that both דיני ממונות and דיני נפשות require דרישה וחקירה of the witnesses, based on the פסוק 'משפט אחד יהיה לכם.'
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Money cases and capital cases are the same in that witnesses must be carefully questioned, because the פסוק says: 'You shall have one law.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens by saying what money cases and capital cases have in common: the witnesses must be checked carefully in both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think only life-and-death cases deserve thorough questioning of witnesses. The משנה says no: the פסוק 'one law' teaches that the same careful questioning applies to money cases too. This shared rule comes first, and the differences come after.

keyTerms.meaning: Money cases (civil cases about payment or property)
Capital cases (cases where the punishment is death)
Careful questioning of the witnesses to check their testimony
One law, the same procedure for everyone

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as 'money cases and capital cases are the same in everything.' The משנה only says they are equal in דרישה וחקירה. The rest of the משנה lists how they differ.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Both cases of monetary law
and cases of capital law
are equal with regard to inquiry and interrogation of witnesses,
as it is stated: “You shall have one manner of law.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת וְאֶחָד דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both דיני ממונות and דיני נפשות require דרישה וחקירה of witnesses, learned from 'משפט אחד יהיה לכם.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It establishes that careful questioning of witnesses is a basic part of every court case, not just capital ones.

steps.title: The differences begin: money cases need three judges, capital cases need twenty-three
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks what separates the two kinds of cases and gives the first difference: דיני ממונות are judged by 3, דיני נפשות by 23.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between money cases and capital cases? Money cases are judged by three judges, and capital cases by twenty-three.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks 'what is the difference?' to set up a list of contrasts, and then gives the first one: the size of the court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'מה בין' is the משנה's own heading for the list, not a challenge. The first contrast is structural: a capital case needs a much larger בית דין of 23, while a money case needs only 3.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between (opens a list of contrasts)
Three (judges)
Twenty-three (judges), a small סנהדרין

phrases.aramaic: מָה בֵּין דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת לְדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת?
phrases.english: What are the differences between cases of monetary law and cases of capital law?
Cases of monetary law are judged by three judges,
and cases of capital law by twenty-three judges.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה בֵּין דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת לְדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the shared rule, the משנה turns to listing differences.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דיני ממונות are judged by 3 judges; דיני נפשות by 23.

steps.title: How deliberation may open: either way in money cases, only for acquittal in capital cases
steps.stepSummary: In דיני ממונות the judges may open with an argument for either side; in דיני נפשות they must open with an argument לזכות, never לחובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In money cases the judges may begin the discussion with an argument to exempt or to obligate. In capital cases they begin with an argument to acquit, and they do not begin with an argument to convict.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second difference: how the judges start their discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a money case, the first argument may favor either side. In a capital case, the discussion must open with a reason to acquit, so the tone of the deliberation starts on the side of saving the accused.

keyTerms.meaning: They open (begin the judges' discussion)
In favor (to exempt or acquit)
Against (to obligate or convict)

phrases.english: In cases of monetary law, the court opens the deliberations
either with a claim to exempt or with a claim to find liable,
and in cases of capital law, the court opens with a claim to acquit
but does not open with a claim to find liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת פּוֹתְחִין בֵּין לִזְכוּת בֵּין לְחוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second item in the list of differences.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Deliberation in דיני ממונות may open either way; in דיני נפשות it opens only לזכות.

steps.title: Majority needed: one vote either way in money cases, but two votes to convict in capital cases
steps.stepSummary: In דיני ממונות a majority of one decides either way. In דיני נפשות a majority of one is enough to acquit, but a majority of two is needed to convict.
steps.simpleTranslation: In money cases the ruling follows a majority of one, whether to exempt or to obligate. In capital cases a majority of one is enough to acquit, but a majority of two is needed to convict.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the third difference: how big a majority the judges need to reach a ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A simple majority of one works for any money ruling. For a capital case, conviction is harder: it needs a majority of two judges. Acquittal still needs only one.

keyTerms.meaning: They tilt or direct (the ruling, by majority vote)
By (a majority of) one
By (a majority of) two

phrases.aramaic: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת – מַטִּין עַל פִּי אֶחָד,
phrases.english: In cases of monetary law, the court decides based on a majority of one judge,
either to exempt or to find liable,

phrases.aramaic: וְדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת – מַטִּין עַל פִּי אֶחָד לִזְכוּת,
phrases.english: but in cases of capital law, the court decides based on a majority of one to acquit,
and based on a majority of two to find liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת מַטִּין עַל פִּי אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third item in the list of differences.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money cases are decided by a majority of one either way; capital cases need a majority of one to acquit and two to convict.

steps.title: Reopening a case: either way in money cases, only for acquittal in capital cases
steps.stepSummary: In דיני ממונות the case may be brought back for retrial in either direction. In דיני נפשות it may be brought back only לזכות, not לחובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In money cases the court may bring the case back to be judged again, whether to exempt or to obligate. In capital cases it brings the case back to acquit, but not to convict.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the fourth difference in this section: whether a case can be reopened after a ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A money ruling can be reopened and changed in either direction. A capital case can be reopened only to help the accused, never to make things worse for him. This fits the pattern of the whole list: capital cases lean toward acquittal.

keyTerms.meaning: They bring back (reopen the case for judgment again)

steps.whatToRemember: There is one shared rule, דרישה וחקירה in both kinds of cases. The differences so far are: 3 vs. 23 judges; who may open the discussion; the majority needed; and reopening the case. In every one of these differences, דיני נפשות lean לזכות, toward saving the accused.

phrases.english: In cases of monetary law, the court brings the case back to be judged again
either to exempt or to find liable,
in cases of capital law, the court brings it back to acquit
but does not bring it back to find liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת מַחְזִירִין בֵּין לִזְכוּת בֵּין לְחוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth item in the list of differences.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A money case may be reopened either way; a capital case may be reopened only to acquit.

steps.title: Who may offer an argument
steps.stepSummary: In דיני ממונות anyone present may argue for either side. In דיני נפשות anyone may argue for acquittal, but not everyone may argue for conviction.
steps.simpleTranslation: In money cases, everyone may offer a reason to clear or to make liable. In capital cases, everyone may offer a reason to acquit, but not everyone may offer a reason to convict.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another difference between the two kinds of cases. This one is about who is allowed to speak up with an argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In money cases, the right to argue is equal in both directions. In capital cases, the door is wide open for anyone who wants to help the accused, but arguing for conviction is limited. The usual explanation is that only the judges themselves may argue for conviction.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone. Here it means all those present at the trial.
Teach. Here it means offering an argument or reason.
Merit. An argument that helps the accused, to clear or acquit him.
Liability. An argument against the accused, to make him liable or convict him.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this with step 3. Step 3 was about which side the judges open with. This step is about WHO may argue at all.

phrases.english: Money cases:
everyone may teach a reason to clear or to make liable,
phrases.notes: "Everyone" means anyone at the trial, even someone who is not one of the judges.

phrases.english: capital cases:
everyone may teach a reason to acquit,
but not everyone may teach a reason to convict.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת – הַכֹּל מְלַמְּדִין זְכוּת וְחוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another difference to the list that began in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In דיני נפשות anyone may argue לזכות, but not everyone may argue לחובה.

steps.title: Switching sides after giving an argument
steps.stepSummary: In דיני ממונות a person may switch his argument in either direction. In דיני נפשות one who argued for conviction may switch to acquittal, but one who argued for acquittal may not switch to conviction.
steps.simpleTranslation: In money cases, one who argued for liability may switch to clearing, and one who argued for clearing may switch to liability. In capital cases, one who argued for conviction may switch to acquittal, but one who argued for acquittal cannot go back and argue for conviction.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the next difference. It is about whether someone who already argued one way may change his mind and argue the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In money cases, changing sides works both ways. In capital cases it only works in the direction that helps the accused. Once someone has spoken in favor of acquittal, he cannot turn around and argue for conviction.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who teaches. Here it means the person who gave an argument.
To go back. Here it means to reverse one's position.

phrases.english: Money cases:
one who taught liability may teach a reason to clear,
and one who taught a reason to clear may teach liability.
Capital cases:
one who taught a reason to convict may teach a reason to acquit,
but one who taught a reason to acquit
cannot go back and teach a reason to convict.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת – הַמְלַמֵּד חוֹבָה מְלַמֵּד זְכוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list. Step 6 asked who may argue, and this step asks whether one may switch arguments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In דיני נפשות one who argued לזכות may not reverse and argue לחובה.

steps.title: Finishing the case at night
steps.stepSummary: Both kinds of cases are judged by day. דיני ממונות may be concluded at night, but דיני נפשות must be concluded by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: In money cases, the court judges by day and may finish at night. In capital cases, the court judges by day and must finish by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from rules about arguments to rules about timing. Here it discusses whether the verdict may be given at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both kinds of cases start in the daytime, so the difference is only about finishing. A money case may run past nightfall and end with a verdict at night. A capital case may not, so its verdict must be given while it is still day.

keyTerms.meaning: They judge. Here it means beginning and hearing the case.
They finish. Here it means concluding and giving the verdict.
In the daytime.
At night.

phrases.english: Money cases:
they judge in the daytime, and may finish at night.
Capital cases:
they judge in the daytime, and finish in the daytime.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת – דָּנִין בַּיּוֹם, וְגוֹמְרִין בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from rules about arguments to rules about the time of the verdict.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דיני נפשות must be concluded during the day, while דיני ממונות may be concluded at night.

steps.title: Waiting a day before a guilty verdict
steps.stepSummary: In דיני ממונות the verdict may be given on the same day in either direction. In דיני נפשות an acquittal may be given the same day, but a conviction must wait until the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: In money cases, the court may finish on the same day, whether to clear or to make liable. In capital cases, the court may finish on the same day to acquit, but only on the following day to convict.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another timing rule. This one is about whether the verdict may be given on the same day the case was heard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8 the question was day versus night. Here the question is same day versus next day. A capital case may end quickly only if the accused is acquitted. A conviction needs an extra day.

keyTerms.meaning: On that same day.
That comes after it. Together with בַּיּוֹם it means the following day.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 8. Step 8 is about night versus day. This step is about the same day versus the next day.

phrases.english: Money cases:
they may finish on that same day,
whether to clear or to make liable.
Capital cases:
they may finish on that same day to acquit,
but only on the following day to convict.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת – גּוֹמְרִין בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם, בֵּין לִזְכוּת בֵּין לְחוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the timing rules from step 8, now comparing the same day with the next day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In דיני נפשות a guilty verdict may only be given on the day after the case was heard.

steps.title: No capital trials before שבת or יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: Because a conviction must wait a day, capital cases are not judged on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, the court does not judge capital cases on the day before שבת or the day before יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה draws a practical result from the rule in step 9. The word לפיכך shows that this rule comes from what was just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A conviction must be given on the following day. If the trial began on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב, the following day would be שבת or יום טוב, when the court does not finish the case. So the court avoids starting capital cases on those days.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore. It shows that a rule follows from the previous one.
The day before שבת.
The day before a festival.

steps.whatToRemember: Every difference in this list follows one pattern: דיני ממונות treat both directions equally, while דיני נפשות lean toward saving the accused. The ban on judging capital cases on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב is a direct result of the next-day rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the משנה builds rules on each other. One rule, waiting a day to convict, creates a new rule about the court's schedule.

phrases.english: Therefore, they do not judge
phrases.notes: He means capital cases, since those are the ones that might need a second day.

phrases.english: neither on the eve of Shabbat
nor on the eve of a festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִיכָךְ, אֵין דָּנִין לֹא בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וְלֹא בְּעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical result from step 9's rule that a conviction must wait until the next day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Capital cases are not judged on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב, because a conviction would have to be given on the following day.

steps.title: Which judge speaks first
steps.stepSummary: In money cases and in questions of טומאה and טהרה, the most senior judge speaks first. In capital cases, the junior judges at the side speak first.
steps.simpleTranslation: In money cases and in questions of impurity and purity, we start with the greatest judge. In capital cases, we start from the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another difference between דיני ממונות and דיני נפשות: the order in which the judges state their opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In money cases and in matters of טומאה and טהרה, the senior judge goes first. In capital cases the junior judges, who sit at the side, go first. This continues the משנה's list of differences between the two kinds of cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Money cases
Capital cases (life-and-death cases)
Questions of ritual impurity and purity
From the greatest (most senior) judge
From the side, where the junior judges sit

phrases.english: Money cases, and impurity and purity questions:
we start from the greatest judge.
Capital cases: we start from the side.
phrases.notes: "The side" is where the less senior judges sit, so they give their opinions first.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת, הַטְּמָאוֹת וְהַטְּהָרוֹת מַתְחִילִין מִן הַגָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of differences between money cases and capital cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money cases and טומאה/טהרה questions start with the senior judge. Capital cases start with the junior judges.

steps.title: Who is fit to judge capital cases
steps.stepSummary: Anyone may judge money cases. Only כהנים, לויים, and ישראלים whose families are fit to marry into כהונה may judge capital cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone is fit to judge money cases. Not everyone is fit to judge capital cases: only כהנים, לויים, and ישראלים who may marry their daughters to כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes its list with one last difference: who is allowed to sit as a judge in each kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For money cases there is no special family requirement. For capital cases the judges must come from families with fit lineage. That means כהנים, לויים, or ישראלים whose daughters may marry a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to judge
Who may marry off their daughters to כהנים, meaning their lineage is fit
The priesthood

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's differences between money cases and capital cases cover who argues, who may switch sides, timing, the order of speaking, and who may judge. Capital cases always get more protection for the accused and stricter requirements.

phrases.english: All are fit to judge money cases,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִין לָדוּן דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת,
phrases.english: but not all are fit to judge capital cases,
only כהנים, לויים,
and ישראלים who marry off their daughters into the priesthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final difference in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone may judge money cases. Only people of fit lineage may judge capital cases.

steps.title: Do money cases really need careful questioning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether money cases really need דרישה וחקירה, and brings a ברייתא about a loan document whose witnesses were challenged about the date.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Do we really need careful questioning in money cases? Compare this ברייתא: A loan document is dated the first of ניסן in the שמיטה year. Other witnesses come and say to the signing witnesses, "How can you testify about this document? On that very day you were with us in such-and-such a place!" The document is still valid, and its witnesses are still fit. We are concerned that perhaps they delayed and wrote it later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by questioning the משנה's statement that money cases need careful questioning of witnesses. It brings a ברייתא to set up a contradiction, which it will spell out in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that when witnesses are shown to have been elsewhere on the date written in the document, we do not cancel the document. We assume the document may have been written later than the loan, with the later date on it. This suggests the court does not pin down the exact date in money matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Careful questioning of witnesses about the exact details, such as time and place
"And contrast them," the formula for raising a contradiction from another source
A written document, here a loan document
We are concerned / we take into account the possibility
They delayed and wrote it, meaning they wrote it after the loan with a later date

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not treat the signing witnesses as liars. Since the document may simply have been written later than the loan, the date alone does not prove false testimony.

phrases.english: גמרא:

phrases.aramaic: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת מִי בָּעֵינַן דְּרִישָׁה וַחֲקִירָה?
phrases.english: Money cases: do we really require careful questioning?
And raise a contradiction:
A document whose date is written
as the first of ניסן in the שמיטה year,
and witnesses came and said:
"How can you testify about this document?

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא בְּיוֹם פְּלוֹנִי עִמָּנוּ הֱיִיתֶם בְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי!״
phrases.english: Weren't you with us on that day in such-and-such a place!"
The document is valid and its witnesses are fit.
We are concerned that perhaps they delayed and wrote it.
phrases.notes: The loan happened earlier, and they wrote and signed the document later, putting the later date on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת מִי בָּעֵינַן דְּרִישָׁה וַחֲקִירָה? וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא by challenging the משנה's rule that money cases need דרישה וחקירה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that money cases require דרישה וחקירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא keeps a document valid even when the witnesses could not have been there on its date. This suggests the exact date is not checked in money matters.

steps.title: Spelling out the contradiction
steps.stepSummary: If money cases needed careful questioning, the witnesses would be asked the exact date, and we could not just assume the document was written late.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think we require careful questioning in money cases, how can we say we are concerned that perhaps they delayed and wrote it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly why the ברייתא contradicts the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With דרישה וחקירה, the court would ask the signing witnesses on which day they signed. Their answer would not match the date on the document, and the testimony would fall apart. The ברייתא instead simply assumes a later writing date, which shows no such questioning is done.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind, meaning "if you were to think"
How

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that we require careful questioning,
how can we be concerned
that perhaps they delayed and wrote it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בָּעֵינַן דְּרִישָׁה וַחֲקִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the logic of the contradiction set up by the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement of דרישה וחקירה in money cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Questioning would expose the date problem and cancel the testimony. Yet the ברייתא assumes a later writing date and keeps the document valid, so no questioning must be required.

steps.title: Why not ask from the משנה about postdated documents?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that a משנה in שביעית, which says postdated loan documents are valid, should already have raised the same difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to your thinking, the משנה should also bother you: loan documents dated too early are invalid, and documents dated too late are valid. If we require careful questioning in money cases, why would a late-dated document be valid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the earlier challenge was taken from a ברייתא, when a משנה seems to make the same point. A משנה carries more weight than a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A postdated document does not match the real date of the loan. If money cases needed exact questioning, that mismatch should disqualify it. Yet the משנה says it is valid, so the משנה seems to be the more obvious source for the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning
Loan documents
Antedated: dated earlier than the real loan
Postdated: dated later than the real loan
If it enters your mind (to say)

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
the משנה should be difficult for you:
Antedated loan documents are invalid,
and postdated ones are valid.
And if it enters your mind
that we require careful questioning,
why are postdated ones valid?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the challenge in steps 13-14 used a ברייתא instead of a stronger-ranking משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of the ברייתא as the source of the challenge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה outranks a ברייתא, and the משנה about postdated documents already seems to show that money cases are not strictly questioned.

steps.title: The ברייתא makes an even stronger point
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא was chosen because it proves the point more strongly. Even on the first of ניסן in שמיטה, when postdating seems unlikely, we still assume the document may have been postdated and accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is no difficulty. We are bringing a stronger proof than the משנה. In the ברייתא, even on the first of ניסן in the שמיטה year, people do not usually lend money, and you would not expect anyone to delay the date and hurt his own document. Even so, since שביעית cancels debts only at its end, we accept the document as valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it used the ברייתא: the ברייתא shows the point in a harder case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Postdating into the שמיטה year moves the loan closer to the year that cancels debts, so a lender would not want to do it. Still, the ברייתא assumes the document may have been postdated, because שמיטה cancels debts only at the end of the year. Accepting the document even here is a stronger sign that money cases are not strictly questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: Stronger than it, a better proof
The seventh year, which cancels loans
Who lend money
Weakens his own document
Cancels debts only at its end

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not solve the main difficulty. It only explains why the ברייתא was a better source than the משנה. The main question returns in the next step.

phrases.english: This is not difficult,
for we are saying something stronger than it.
For even on the first of Nisan in the Sabbatical Year,
when people who lend are not common,
where one cannot easily say 'perhaps they delayed and wrote it,'
since a person would not weaken his own document,
even so,
since the Seventh Year cancels debts only at its end,
we deem it valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, דַּעֲדִיפָא מִינַּהּ קָאָמְרִינַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: The source with the stronger case was chosen on purpose.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה would have been the better source for the challenge.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא shows the leniency even where postdating is unlikely, so it is the stronger proof.

steps.title: The difficulty still stands, plus a memory aid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the main contradiction, which is still unresolved, and gives the memory aid חרפ״ש for the answers that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, it is difficult. Memory aid: חרפ״ש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the original contradiction from steps 13-14 is still a real difficulty. It is setting up the list of answers that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The side discussion only explained why the ברייתא was used. The real problem remains: our משנה requires דרישה וחקירה in money cases, but the ברייתא does not. The letters חרפ״ש stand for the names of the חכמים who will each offer an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, either way
A memory aid

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult.
Mnemonic: Ḥet, Reish, Peh, Shin.
phrases.notes: Each letter stands for the name of a חכם who gives an answer next. The first is ח, for רבי חנינא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side question about the ברייתא and returns to the main contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's rule that money cases require דרישה וחקירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא accepts loan documents without exact questioning about the date.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: Torah law requires it, but the חכמים eased it for lenders
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says that by Torah law both money cases and capital cases need דרישה וחקירה. The חכמים removed this in money cases so that people will not stop lending.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: By Torah law, both money cases and capital cases need careful questioning, as it says, 'You shall have one law.' Why did they say money cases do not need careful questioning? So as not to lock the door in front of borrowers.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer to the contradiction. Our משנה reflects Torah law, and the ברייתא reflects a later ruling of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'one law' puts money cases and capital cases on the same level, so strict questioning applies to both. If witnesses were questioned this closely about loans, small contradictions would often cancel their testimony. Lenders would struggle to collect and would stop lending, so the חכמים waived the requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
One law (ויקרא 24:22)
Lock the door
Borrowers

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the leniency in money cases is a rule of the חכמים made for practical reasons. It is not a basic difference in Torah law between money cases and capital cases.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי חנינא, the Torah requires דרישה וחקירה in all cases. The חכמים waived it in money cases to keep lending available.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina says:
By Torah law,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת וְאֶחָד דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת
phrases.english: both monetary cases and capital cases
require inquiry and interrogation,
as it is stated: 'You shall have one manner of law.'
And what is the reason they said

phrases.aramaic: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת לָא בָּעֵינַן דְּרִישָׁה וַחֲקִירָה?
phrases.english: that in monetary cases we do not need inquiry and interrogation?

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תִּנְעוֹל דֶּלֶת בִּפְנֵי לֹוִין.
phrases.english: So as not to lock the door in the face of borrowers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer (ח of חרפ״ש) to the difficulty stated again in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two sources reflect two levels of law: Torah law and a ruling of the חכמים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה and the ברייתא contradict each other about questioning in money cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה states Torah law. The ברייתא reflects the חכמים' leniency, made so that people will keep lending.

steps.title: Opening a challenge to רבי חנינא's answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge with 'אלא מעתה', meaning: if what רבי חנינא said is true, then something strange should follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so (that the חכמים removed careful questioning in money cases)...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It accepts רבי חנינא's idea for a moment so it can show a problem that comes from it; the problem itself is stated at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא said that by Torah law money cases also need דרישה וחקירה, and the חכמים dropped it so lending would not stop. 'אלא מעתה' signals that the גמרא will now push this idea further and show it leads to a result that seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so / from now on (if we accept this idea): a phrase that opens a challenge by drawing out a problem from what was just said
Careful, detailed questioning of the witnesses

steps.confusionAlert: אלא מעתה does not ask a question by itself. It is only the opening of a challenge, and the actual difficulty comes at the start of the next amud.

phrases.english: But if that is so
phrases.notes: He means: if the חכמים really removed careful questioning in money cases, as רבי חנינא just said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge against the answer of רבי חנינא in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's claim that the חכמים removed דרישה וחקירה in money cases so people will not stop lending.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Accept the claim for a moment and draw out a result from it that seems unacceptable; the specific result is stated in the following line.
